$$30V^2 + 400V - 70000 = 0 \implies 3V^2 + 40V - 7000 = 0$$

walkthrough.text:
Solve the quadratic equation $3V^2 + 40V - 7000 = 0$ using the quadratic formula:
$$V = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \frac{-40 \pm \sqrt{40^2 - 4(3)(-7000)}}{2(3)}$$
$$V = \frac{-40 \pm \sqrt{1600 + 84000}}{6} = \frac{-40 \pm \sqrt{85600}}{6}$$
$$\sqrt{85600} \approx 292.5748$$

Select the physically meaningful positive root:
$$V = \frac{-40 + 292.5748}{6} = \frac{252.5748}{6} \approx 42.0958\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 42.1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the driving force at maximum speed:
$$F = \frac{P}{V} = \frac{70000}{42.0958} \approx 1662.87\text{ N} \approx 1660\text{ N} \quad (1.66\text{ kN})$$
Equivalently, $R = 400 + 30(42.0958) = 1662.87\text{ N} \approx 1660\text{ N}$.

- Thrust matches drag at top speed:
$$F = \frac{70000}{42.1} \approx 1660\text{ N}$$
The car reaches $42.1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with an engine thrust of $1660\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Towing combination with emergency towbar break on level road

hints: Driving force at $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is $F = \frac{54000}{15} = 3600\text{ N}$.
Combined mass is $3000 + 1800 = 4800\text{ kg}$ and total drag is $600 + 400 = 1000\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the van: $T - 400 = 1800(0.54167) = 975 \implies T = 1375\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the driving force developed by the truck at $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{54000}{15} = 3600\text{ N} \quad (3.6\text{ kN})$$

Apply Newton's second law to the combined system ($m_{\text{total}} = 4800\text{ kg}$):
$$F - R_{\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$3600 - (600 + 400) = 4800a \implies 2600 = 4800a$$
$$a = \frac{2600}{4800} = \frac{13}{24}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.5417\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.542\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the van alone to find towbar tension $T$:
$$T - R_{\text{van}} = m_{\text{van}} a$$
$$T - 400 = (1800)\left(\frac{13}{24}\right) = 975 \implies T = 1375\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine system parameters at $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
- Truck driving thrust:
$$F = \frac{54000}{15} = 3600\text{ N}$$
- Combined rig acceleration:
$$a = \frac{3600 - 1000}{4800} = \frac{13}{24} \approx 0.542\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate towbar tension:
- The towbar overcomes van drag and accelerates it:
$$T = 400 + 1800\left(\frac{13}{24}\right) = 1375\text{ N}$$
The towbar experiences $1375\text{ N}$ of tension.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Towing combination with emergency towbar break on level road

hints: Immediately after the towbar breaks, the truck mass is only $3000\text{ kg}$ and its resistance is $600\text{ N}$.
Truck acceleration: $a_{\text{truck}} = \frac{3600 - 600}{3000} = \frac{3000}{3000} = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
For the van, the only horizontal force is its resistance of $400\text{ N}$, decelerating it from $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to rest.
Use work-energy: initial kinetic energy equals work against resistance: $\frac{1}{2}(1800)(15^2) = 400s \implies 202500 = 400s \implies s = 506.25\text{ m} \approx 506\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply Newton's second law to the truck alone immediately after the towbar breaks:
$$F - R_{\text{truck}} = m_{\text{truck}} a_{\text{truck}}$$
$$3600 - 600 = 3000 a_{\text{truck}} \implies 3000 = 3000 a_{\text{truck}} \implies a_{\text{truck}} = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the work-energy principle for the van as it rolls to rest:
$$\Delta E_k = W_{\text{resist}}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}m_{\text{van}} u^2 = R_{\text{van}} s$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(1800)(15^2) = (400)s$$
$$202500 = 400s \implies s = \frac{202500}{400} = 506.25\text{ m} \approx 506\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the freed truck:
- Released from towing load, thrust of $3600\text{ N}$ only opposes $600\text{ N}$:
$$a_{\text{truck}} = \frac{3600 - 600}{3000} = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate van stopping distance:
- Kinetic energy converted into work against friction:
$$\frac{1}{2}(1800)(15^2) = 400s \implies 202500 = 400s$$
$$s = 506.25\text{ m} \approx 506\text{ m}$$
The van coasts $506\text{ m}$ to a halt.
